s: The First Amendment ("Congress shall make no law… abridging the freedom of speech, or of the press") applies to all government actors through incorporation (Gitlow, 1925).
It does not apply to private actors: employers, private universities and platforms are not bound (Manhattan Community Access v. Halleck, 2019).
Platforms' own editorial choices are themselves protected expression (Moody v. NetChoice, 2024).
Is the activity speech or expressive conduct?
Is it within an unprotected or less-protected category?
Is the regulation content-based (including viewpoint-based) or content-neutral?
Apply forum analysis on government property.
Is there a special context: government employment, schools, government speech, subsidies, prisons, the military?
Apply the appropriate scrutiny and check vagueness and overbreadth.

A law that prohibits a substantial amount of protected speech relative to its legitimate sweep is facially invalid, even as applied to someone whose own speech is unprotected (United States v. Stevens, 2010; United States v. Hansen, 2023).
Vague laws chill speech and invite arbitrary enforcement.

When the government speaks, it may choose its message, so the Free Speech Clause does not apply (Pleasant Grove City v. Summum, 2009; Walker v. Texas Division, 2015, license plates; compare Shurtleff v. Boston, 2022, flag-raising program not government speech).
